segments.text: Aggregation: from many rows to a single value, for a whole table or for each group.
Think of a supermarket receipt: many lines above, and one total at the bottom.
An aggregate function does the same with rows. Count star and the average grade turn six enrolments into a single row.
Count star counts rows. On the student table, that is three.
Count of email counts only the values that are not NULL. Eva has no email, so the answer is two.
To count values that may be missing, count the column, not the rows.
Sum, average, minimum and maximum work the same way, here over the grades of enrolment.
The lowest grade is five, the highest nine, the total forty-three point five, and the average seven point two five.
They also skip NULLs: a missing grade is not a zero.
Now, an average for each course. GROUP BY is like sorting the laundry into piles.
Group by course id makes one pile per course: three rows for C ten, two for C eleven, and one for C twenty.
Then the aggregates are computed for each pile, and every pile becomes one row of the result.
C ten has three students and an average of six point six seven. C eleven, eight point two five. C twenty, seven.
There are two places to filter. WHERE filters rows, before grouping: here, grades under six are dropped.
Eva's five in C ten never reaches a pile.
HAVING filters groups, after grouping. Having count star at least two throws away the whole C twenty pile.
Two courses remain, C ten and C eleven, each with two grades of six or more.
Conditions on aggregates go in HAVING. Everything else, in WHERE.
It all follows from the logical order: FROM, then WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, then SELECT, and finally ORDER BY.
WHERE runs before the groups exist, so it cannot use an aggregate. ORDER BY runs last, so it can use the aliases of the SELECT.
Three errors you will meet. A plain column next to an aggregate, without GROUP BY: O R A zero zero nine three seven, not a single-group group function.
Every column outside an aggregate must be in the GROUP BY. If not: O R A zero zero nine seven nine.
And an aggregate in WHERE gives O R A zero zero nine three four. Move it to HAVING.
Practise it in the SQL section of the course site.
